# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

**Football Player Performance Report** — a Python static HTML generator for Baylor Athletics' B.A.I.R. Initiative. Reads from three existing DuckDB pipelines, computes TSA (Total Score of Athleticism) composite scores, and renders a self-contained interactive HTML report.

**Run it:**
```bash
python generate_report.py --start 2025-09-01 --end 2026-03-28 --label "Spring 2026"
# Output: output/Spring_2026_2026-03-28.html
```

> The original React + FastAPI spec has been replaced by this approach. Reference specs are in `docs/` (TECH_SPEC.md, UI_WIREFRAMES.md, DATA_SCHEMA.md, TSA_METHODOLOGY.md) and do not reflect the implementation.

---

## Commands

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Generate a report for a date range
python generate_report.py --start YYYY-MM-DD --end YYYY-MM-DD --label "Label"

# Override output path
python generate_report.py --start 2025-09-01 --end 2026-03-28 --label "Spring 2026" --output out/custom.html

# Upstream pipelines: on the Mac, launchd pulls GPS, Perch and VALD on a schedule
# (com.keystone.gpspull, perchpull, valdpull). By hand:
# python ~/DEV/ForcePlate_DecisionSystem/src/ingest/pipeline.py
# cd ~/DEV/DataBase_GPS_Reporting/gps_report && python bulk_import.py --start 2025-09-01 --end <date>
# python src/perch_ingest.py --start 2025-09-01 --end <date>
```

---

## Architecture

```
generate_report.py      # CLI entry: argparse -> data -> score -> render -> write HTML
config.py               # absolute paths to all 5 data sources + output dir
src/
  data.py               # load_cmj(), load_gps(), load_bodyweight(), load_imtp(), load_perch(), merge_all()
  scorer.py             # z->t per metric, 5 domain composites, TSA, RAG
  renderer.py           # serialize DataFrame to JSON, render Jinja2 template
  perch_ingest.py       # Perch API client → data/perch.duckdb cache (run separately)
templates/
  report.html.j2        # dark-theme HTML: Chart.js radar (9 axes) + sortable table + inline JS
data/
  athlete_roster.csv    # 98 active athletes: full_name, jersey_number, position, catapult_id, forcedecks_id
  perch.duckdb          # Perch 1RM cache (not committed; populate with src/perch_ingest.py)
output/                 # generated HTML files (not committed)
```

## Data Sources

| Source | Path | Status |
|--------|------|--------|
| ForcePlate DB | `~/DEV/ForcePlate_DecisionSystem/data/forceplate.db` | Built |
| GPS DB | `~/DEV/DataBase_GPS_Reporting/gps_report/data/gps_history.duckdb` | Built |
| Body Weight CSV | `~/DEV/Football/FootballBodyWeightDevelopment/BodyWeightMaster.csv` (BodWeightWeb archived) | Built |
| Roster crosswalk | `data/athlete_roster.csv` | Built |
| Perch DB | `data/perch.duckdb` (local cache, populated by `src/perch_ingest.py`) | **Built** |

**GPS pipeline note:** `bulk_import.py` imports data into the DB; `run_report.py` only generates reports from existing data — do not confuse them.

**ForcePlate DB tables used:** `raw_tests` (CMJ metrics), `classified_athletes` (mRSI + CMJ classification), `imtp_tests` (IMTP metrics). IMTP data is ingested via the ForcePlate pipeline (`ForcePlate_DecisionSystem/src/ingest/pipeline.py`).

**All paths are defined in `config.py`.** Change them there if pipelines move.

## TSA Scoring (9 axes, 5 domains)

| Domain | Metric | Source | Field |
|--------|--------|--------|-------|
| CMJ | Jump Height (cm) | `raw_tests` | `"Jump Height (Imp-Mom)"` |
| CMJ | Peak Power / BM (W/kg) | `raw_tests` | `"Peak Power / BM"` |
| CMJ | mRSI | `classified_athletes` | `mrsi` |
| GPS | High Speed Distance (m) | `athlete_sessions` | `high_speed_distance_m` |
| GPS | Player Load | `athlete_sessions` | `total_player_load` |
| GPS | Max Velocity (m/s) | `athlete_sessions` | `max_velocity_ms` |
| BW  | Body Weight (kg) | `BodyWeightMaster.csv` | WEIGHT x 0.453592 |
| Strength | Peak Force / BM (N/kg) | `imtp_tests` | `"Peak Vertical Force / BM"` |
| Weight Room | Back Squat 1RM/BW | `perch.duckdb` | 1RM (lbs) ÷ BW (lbs) |
| Weight Room | Power Clean 1RM/BW | `perch.duckdb` | 1RM (lbs) ÷ BW (lbs) |
| Weight Room | Bench Press 1RM/BW | `perch.duckdb` | 1RM (lbs) ÷ BW (lbs) |
| Weight Room | Hang Power Clean 1RM/BW | `perch.duckdb` | 1RM (lbs) ÷ BW (lbs) |

**Display-only IMTP metrics** (shown in profile panel, not in TSA domain score): Peak Force (N), RFD 0–100ms (N/s), RFD 0–200ms (N/s).

**Scoring:** z-score per metric (population = all athletes with that metric) -> t-score (z*10+50, clipped 0-100) -> domain mean (CMJ avg of 3, GPS avg of 3, BW = weight_t, Strength = peak_force_bm_t, Weight Room = mean of up to 4 exercise t-scores) -> TSA = mean of available domains (partial domain scores allowed for Weight Room).

**Weight Room radar axis:** single composite score (`weight_room_domain`); individual exercise 1RMs shown in profile panel only. Athletes without Perch data score from the remaining 4 domains; "Weight Room" shown in missing_domains note.

**RAG:** roster-relative -- top 33% green, middle 34% amber, bottom 33% red.

**Missing domain handling:** athletes missing any domain still get a TSA from available domains; a note appears in their profile panel.

## Perch API Integration (pipeline verified and data ingested 2026-04-25)

**API base:** `https://api.perch.fit` — Bearer token auth (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`).

**Ingest script:** `src/perch_ingest.py` — run before generating the report:
```bash
python src/perch_ingest.py --probe                              # verify connectivity (no dates needed)
python src/perch_ingest.py --start 2025-09-01 --end 2026-03-28 # full ingest
```

**Data source:** `POST /v3/sets` filtered by `exercise_id` — NOT `/stats` (which returns empty). 1RM is computed as `weight / pct_1rm` per set where `pct_1rm` is set (0–1 decimal). Records are newest-first; ingest stops paginating when `created_at` falls before `start_date`.

**Exercise IDs (confirmed):** Back Squat=1, Bench Press=2, Power Clean=19, Hang Power Clean=48. Defined in `_EXERCISE_ID_MAP` at top of `src/perch_ingest.py`.

**Users endpoint:** `POST /v2/users` with `{"group_id": org_id}`. Org ID resolved dynamically from `GET /v2/user` → `data.org_id` (Baylor = 959).

**Exercises tracked:** back squat, power clean, bench press, hang power clean.

**Metric:** 1RM computed from `weight / pct_1rm` per set, normalized by bodyweight (1RM ÷ BW, both lbs).

**Athlete join:** name-match from Perch `/v2/users` (first_name + last_name) to `athlete_roster.csv` full_name using `_normalize_name()`.

**API token:** stored in `.env` as `PERCH_API_TOKEN` (never committed). Copy `.env.example` → `.env` to get started.

## Scheduled pull and Parquet snapshots (Mac owns perch.duckdb)

The Mac is the only writer of `data/perch.duckdb`: launchd `com.keystone.perchpull` runs `pull_perch.sh`
(10:05 + 16:35). After a successful ingest, `pull_perch.sh` runs `export_snapshot.py` (logic in
`src/snapshot.py`), which opens the DB read-only and writes Parquet to Google Drive for Windows:

- **Where:** `$ATHLETE_SNAPSHOT_DIR/perch/`, else `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/athlete-snapshots/perch/`
  (Mac `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/...`, Windows `G:\My Drive\...`).
  `perch_1rm.parquet` + `manifest.json` (per table: rows, bytes, written_at UTC, machine, newest `test_date`).
- **Windows reads, never writes:**
  `duckdb.sql("select * from 'G:/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/athlete-snapshots/perch/perch_1rm.parquet'")`.
- **Atomic:** written as `<table>.parquet.tmp`, then renamed.
- **Stale-writer guard:** a table whose snapshot already records more rows than this DB is refused (exit 3)
  unless `--force`. `perch_1rm` deletes and re-inserts per key, so its count never legitimately drops.
- **Failure:** exit 0 ok · 1 error · 2 no DB / Drive not mounted · 3 refused. Non-zero alerts
  (`snapshot-export exit=N`) and is recorded in `logs/last_run.json` under `snapshot_export`; the pull's
  exit code is unchanged.
- **By hand (Mac):** `.venv/bin/python export_snapshot.py --dry-run`, then without `--dry-run`.

## Athlete Roster

`data/athlete_roster.csv` is the join key between all three pipelines. **Do not delete it.**

- 98 active athletes; all have ForcePlate data
- 83 also have a Catapult GPS ID; 15 are not yet in Catapult
- Jersey numbers are mostly blank -- fill manually for UI display
- Joins: ForcePlate on `forcedecks_id`, GPS on `catapult_id`, BW on normalized `full_name`

To add new athletes or update IDs, edit `data/athlete_roster.csv` directly.

## What Is Not Yet Built

See [CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md) for full detail. Key deferred items:

- **Perch / Weight Room domain** -- Fully implemented (2026-04-24). Run `src/perch_ingest.py --probe` first time to verify API field names, then full ingest. Once `data/perch.duckdb` is populated the Weight Room domain activates automatically.
- **Dual y-axes in trend detail charts** -- RFD (N/s) and Peak Force/BM (N/kg) share a single y-axis; add secondary axis when Chart.js dual-axis is wired up
- **Athlete comparison panel** -- side-by-side spider chart overlay
- **BW fallback** -- Fully implemented (2026-04-25). `_load_fd_bw()` and `_load_bw_combined()` in `src/data.py` fill gaps using `"Bodyweight in Kilograms"` from `raw_tests`. CSV wins; FD fills NaN. Wired into `merge_all()`, `load_perch()`, `load_perch_history()`.
- **Position-specific normalization** -- v1 uses full-roster z-scores
- **Jersey numbers** -- need manual entry in `data/athlete_roster.csv`

## Downstream Projects

**Risk_Stratification_Engine** (`~/DEV/Risk_Stratification_Engine/`) reads the same canonical DB files through its `config/paths.local.yaml`.

**PerformanceSnapshot** (`~/DEV/Football/PerformanceSnapshot/`, 2026-10-29) reads `data/perch.duckdb` read-only (`perch_1rm`: name_normalized, exercise, one_rm_lbs, test_date). It is the successor for player profiles: STEN by position across Winter / Summer / In-season. This repo stays the Perch pull host.

## Git Conventions

- Branches: `main` (stable) -> `dev` (active) -> `feature/*`
- Commit prefixes: `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `data:`, `docs:`
- `.gitignore` excludes: `__pycache__/`, `venv/`, `.env`, `data/*.duckdb`, `data/raw/`

#!/bin/bash
# One command for the Perch pull — the 10:00 + 16:30 launchd job and any manual run.
#   ./pull_perch.sh
# Re-fetches the last 14 days of Perch 1RM sets (from the newest test_date already stored)
# into data/perch.duckdb. The ingest is an upsert keyed by athlete/exercise/date, so
# re-fetching a window is safe. Perch sometimes answers 502 mid-pagination; the ingest
# writes nothing until every page is in, so a failed attempt is simply retried.
# Every run leaves logs/last_run.json; a failure appends one line to the alert log that
# the Claude Code SessionStart hook surfaces. Exit code = the last ingest attempt's.
# After a successful ingest it writes Parquet snapshots of every table to Google Drive
# (export_snapshot.py) so the Windows laptop can read the data. An export failure alerts
# and is recorded in the receipt under snapshot_export, but never changes the exit code.
set -u

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PY="${PERCH_PULL_PYTHON:-$HERE/.venv/bin/python}"
SNAPSHOT_DIR="${PERCH_PULL_SNAPSHOT_DIR:-}"  # empty: $ATHLETE_SNAPSHOT_DIR, else Drive
DB="$HERE/data/perch.duckdb"
RECEIPT="$HERE/logs/last_run.json"
ALERT_LOG="${PERCH_PULL_ALERT_LOG:-$HOME/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log}"
SEASON_START="2025-09-01"
WINDOW_DAYS=14
ATTEMPTS=3

stamp() { date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z'; }

alert() {
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$ALERT_LOG")"
  printf '[%s] perch-pull: %s — see %s\n' "$(stamp)" "$1" "$RECEIPT" >> "$ALERT_LOG"
}

if ! cd "$HERE"; then
  alert "error exit=1 cannot cd to $HERE"
  exit 1
fi
mkdir -p "$HERE/logs"

started="$(stamp)"
echo "[$started] perch pull start"

# Window start: newest stored test_date minus WINDOW_DAYS; season start if the DB is empty.
start="$("$PY" -c '
import sys, duckdb
from datetime import timedelta
try:
    c = duckdb.connect(sys.argv[1], read_only=True)
    d = c.execute("select max(test_date) from perch_1rm").fetchone()[0]
except Exception:
    d = None
print((d - timedelta(days=int(sys.argv[2]))).isoformat() if d else sys.argv[3])
' "$DB" "$WINDOW_DAYS" "$SEASON_START")"
end="$(date '+%Y-%m-%d')"
echo "window $start -> $end"

rc=1
attempt=0
while [ "$attempt" -lt "$ATTEMPTS" ]; do
  attempt=$((attempt + 1))
  "$PY" src/perch_ingest.py --start "$start" --end "$end"
  rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && break
  echo "attempt $attempt failed (exit=$rc)"
  [ "$attempt" -lt "$ATTEMPTS" ] && sleep 60
done

"$PY" -c '
import json, sys, duckdb
started, rc, attempts, start, end, db, out = sys.argv[1:8]
rows = newest = None
try:
    c = duckdb.connect(db, read_only=True)
    rows, newest = c.execute("select count(*), max(test_date) from perch_1rm").fetchone()
except Exception:
    pass
json.dump({
    "started_at": started,
    "status": "ok" if rc == "0" else "error",
    "exit_code": int(rc),
    "attempts": int(attempts),
    "window_start": start,
    "window_end": end,
    "db_path": db,
    "db_rows": rows,
    "db_newest_test_date": newest.isoformat() if newest else None,
}, open(out, "w"), indent=2)
' "$started" "$rc" "$attempt" "$start" "$end" "$DB" "$RECEIPT"

if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
  alert "error exit=$rc after $attempt attempt(s)"
fi

# Parquet snapshots for Windows (successful pulls only). Logged + alerted, never fatal.
if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  if [ -n "$SNAPSHOT_DIR" ]; then
    "$PY" "$HERE/export_snapshot.py" --db "$DB" --receipt "$RECEIPT" --dest "$SNAPSHOT_DIR"
  else
    "$PY" "$HERE/export_snapshot.py" --db "$DB" --receipt "$RECEIPT"
  fi
  xrc=$?
  echo "[$(stamp)] snapshot export exit=$xrc"
  if [ "$xrc" -ne 0 ]; then
    alert "snapshot-export exit=$xrc (pull succeeded; Windows snapshot not refreshed)"
  fi
fi
echo "[$(stamp)] perch pull end exit=$rc"
exit "$rc"

name: cloud-push-launchd-blocked
description: "cloud-push under launchd: macOS per-file com.apple.macl blocks it; fixed 2026-10-23 by running it inside Terminal via cloud-push-launch.sh"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 802ea68a-c53e-4d3a-a897-1d311560fdd1
  modified: 2026-10-23T12:24:59.589Z

`com.keystone.clouddrivepush` (07:00 and 17:30) failed under launchd from 2026-10-12 to 10-23 with rsync `open: Operation not permitted` on `Drive/.../_MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV/`. By hand from Terminal it always worked.

**Cause (tested 2026-10-23).** A process started straight by launchd (python3 or bash) can stat, mkdir and create new files in the Drive mount, and rewrite files it made itself. It cannot list Drive folders, or open, rename over, or delete files that Terminal made. Each such file carries `com.apple.macl` naming Terminal; `xattr -d` does not remove it. Full Disk Access on `Python.app`/rsync does not help (tried 10-14). rsync lists the destination, so it failed on the first step.

**Fix (live 2026-10-23).** The plist runs `/bin/bash ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push-launch.sh`. That runs `open -g -a Terminal ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.command`, which runs `cloud-push.py` (rsync, unchanged) with Terminal's access. The launcher waits 90 s for a new `START` line in `cloud-push.log`; if none, it writes an ERROR to the log and to `.errors.log`. Tracked plist copy: `~/.claude/scripts/com.keystone.clouddrivepush.plist`. Proven: kickstarted runs OK 07:15 and 07:21 with the screen locked.

**Known costs.** Each run opens a Terminal window. Eric set profile "Clear Dark" to "Close if the shell exited cleanly" (10-23, in Terminal Settings; a `defaults import` did not reach the running Terminal), so the window closes when the copy ends (tested). Under memory pressure Terminal ran queued opens ~5 min late; the 90 s check would log that as an ERROR even if the copy runs later.

**How to apply:** Do not swap rsync for a launchd-run copier: Terminal-made files can never be updated that way, and a by-hand run re-taints files. By hand is still `python3 ~/.claude/scripts/cloud-push.py`, or `launchctl kickstart gui/501/com.keystone.clouddrivepush`. Off switch: `launchctl bootout gui/501/com.keystone.clouddrivepush`. Any other launchd job that must read or change Terminal-made Drive files hits the same wall; route it through Terminal the same way or use the `gws` API. See [[automation-cadence]] and [[cloud-copy-approval]].

#!/bin/bash
# Rebuild the snapshot and replace the Drive copy. Run by launchd com.keystone.snapshot
# whenever a VALD, GPS or Perch pull writes its logs/last_run.json, plus once at 21:30.
#   ./run_snapshot.sh            # same as the scheduled run
#   SNAPSHOT_WAIT=0 ./run_snapshot.sh
# If another pull is still running it exits 0 and does nothing: that pull's receipt
# starts it again when it finishes. A DuckDB lock (a pull writing) is retried.
# Every run leaves logs/last_run.json; a failure appends one line to the alert log the
# Claude Code SessionStart hook surfaces.
set -u

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PY="$HERE/.venv/bin/python"
RECEIPT="$HERE/logs/last_run.json"
ALERT_LOG="${SNAPSHOT_ALERT_LOG:-$HOME/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log}"
WAIT="${SNAPSHOT_WAIT:-120}"
ATTEMPTS=3

stamp() { date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z'; }
receipt() {
  printf '{\n  "started_at": "%s",\n  "finished_at": "%s",\n  "status": "%s",\n  "exit_code": %s,\n  "attempts": %s,\n  "note": "%s"\n}\n' \
    "$started" "$(stamp)" "$1" "$2" "$attempt" "$3" > "$RECEIPT"
}

cd "$HERE" || exit 1
mkdir -p "$HERE/logs"
started="$(stamp)"
attempt=0
echo "[$started] snapshot start"

sleep "$WAIT"
if pgrep -f 'pull_vald\.sh|gps_report/pull\.sh|pull_perch\.sh' >/dev/null; then
  echo "[$(stamp)] a pull is still running; its receipt will start this again"
  receipt skipped 0 "pull still running"
  exit 0
fi

rc=1
while [ "$attempt" -lt "$ATTEMPTS" ]; do
  attempt=$((attempt + 1))
  out="$("$PY" snapshot.py --upload 2>&1)"
  rc=$?
  echo "$out"
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && break
  echo "attempt $attempt failed (exit=$rc)"
  [ "$attempt" -lt "$ATTEMPTS" ] && sleep 60
done

if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  receipt ok 0 "$(echo "$out" | grep -c 'Drive: ') upload"
else
  last="$(echo "$out" | tail -1 | tr -d '"\\' | cut -c1-200)"
  receipt error "$rc" "$last"
  printf '[%s] performance-snapshot: error exit=%s after %s attempt(s): %s — see %s\n' \
    "$(stamp)" "$rc" "$attempt" "$last" "$RECEIPT" >> "$ALERT_LOG"
fi
echo "[$(stamp)] snapshot end exit=$rc"
exit "$rc"

def name_key(name: str) -> str:
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", re.sub(r"[^a-z ]", "", str(name).strip().lower())).strip()


def _ro(path) -> duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection:
    return duckdb.connect(str(path), read_only=True)


def _fds(table: str, fields: list[str]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    with _ro(config.FORCEPLATE_DB) as c:
        return c.execute(
            f"""SELECT athlete_name AS name, sport, position, test_date AS date,
                       metric_name AS field, metric_value AS value
                FROM {table}
                WHERE {_KEEP_SPORT} AND metric_name IN ({",".join("?" * len(fields))})
                  AND metric_value IS NOT NULL""",
            fields,
        ).df()


def load(cfg: dict) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict[str, str], pd.DataFrame, dict[str, str]]:
    """Returns (long data, name_key -> position group, body weight rows, freshness by source)."""
    by_source = {s: [m["field"] for m in cfg["metrics"] if m["source"] == s]
                 for s in ("cmj", "imtp", "gps", "perch")}
    code_to_group = {code: grp for grp, codes in cfg["positions"].items() for code in codes}

    cmj = _fds("raw_tests", by_source["cmj"] + ["Bodyweight in Kilograms"])
    imtp = _fds("imtp_tests", by_source["imtp"])
    cmj["source"], imtp["source"] = "cmj", "imtp"

    with _ro(config.GPS_DB) as c:
        gps_cols = ", ".join(f"s.{f}" for f in by_source["gps"])
        gps = c.execute(
            f"""SELECT a.name, a.position, s.session_date AS date, {gps_cols}
                FROM athlete_sessions s JOIN athletes a ON a.catapult_id = s.athlete_id"""
        ).df()
    gps = gps.melt(id_vars=["name", "position", "date"], var_name="field", value_name="value")
    gps = gps.dropna(subset=["value"])
    gps["source"] = "gps"
    cap = cfg["gps_max_velocity_cap"]
    gps = gps[~((gps["field"] == "max_velocity_ms") & ((gps["value"] > cap) | (gps["value"] <= 0)))]

    with _ro(config.PERCH_DB) as c:
        perch = c.execute(
            f"""SELECT name_normalized AS name, test_date AS date, exercise AS field,
                       one_rm_lbs AS value
                FROM perch_1rm WHERE exercise IN ({",".join("?" * len(by_source["perch"]))})""",
            by_source["perch"],
        ).df()
    perch["source"] = "perch"

    # Position: Catapult first, then ForceDecks Football overrides (newest test wins).
    pos: dict[str, str] = {}
    for _, r in gps.sort_values("date")[["name", "position"]].drop_duplicates("name", keep="last").iterrows():
        if r["position"] in code_to_group:
            pos[name_key(r["name"])] = code_to_group[r["position"]]
    fds = pd.concat([cmj, imtp])
    fds = fds[fds["position"].isin(code_to_group)].sort_values("date")
    for _, r in fds[["name", "position"]].drop_duplicates("name", keep="last").iterrows():
        pos[name_key(r["name"])] = code_to_group[r["position"]]

    long = pd.concat([cmj, imtp, gps, perch], ignore_index=True)
    aliases = {name_key(k): name_key(v) for k, v in (cfg.get("aliases") or {}).items()}
    long["name_key"] = long["name"].map(name_key).replace(aliases)
    long["date"] = pd.to_datetime(long["date"])
    # Football only: every source keeps just the names with a football position.
    recent = long["date"] >= long["date"].max() - pd.Timedelta(days=120)
    unmatched = sorted(set(long.loc[(long["source"] == "perch") & recent & ~long["name_key"].isin(pos), "name_key"]))
    config.OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (config.OUTPUT_DIR / "unmatched_names.txt").write_text("\n".join(unmatched) + "\n")
    if unmatched:
        print(f"Perch: {len(unmatched)} names in the last 120 days match no football athlete; "
              f"see outputs/unmatched_names.txt, fix in snapshot.yaml aliases")
    long = long[long["name_key"].isin(pos)]

    bw = long[long["field"] == "Bodyweight in Kilograms"][["name_key", "date", "value"]]
    long = long[long["field"] != "Bodyweight in Kilograms"]

    fresh = long.groupby("source")["date"].max().dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d").to_dict()
    return long[["name_key", "name", "date", "source", "field", "value"]], pos, bw, fresh

"""Sport-generic helpers, so the central force plate store can hold more than football.

The classification engine in `src/classify/` is football-specific by construction: it
scores athletes against NFL normative percentiles keyed by football position. Those
norms do not exist for volleyball, and applying them would be worse than useless.

So the split this module enables is deliberate:

  * `raw_tests` is **sport-agnostic** — it is the central store any system can read.
  * `classified_athletes` stays **football only** — it is where the NFL norms are applied.

A sport with no normative reference can still be ingested and analysed within-athlete
(each athlete against her own history), which needs no external norm.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

FOOTBALL = "Football"
VOLLEYBALL = "Volleyball"


def athlete_sport(athlete: dict) -> str | None:
    """The VALD ``Sports`` attribute for an athlete, or None if unset.

    VALD carries sport as a profile attribute rather than a separate tenant — the whole
    department shares one team id — so this is the only thing separating a volleyball
    athlete from a football one.
    """
    for attr in athlete.get("attributes", []):
        if attr.get("typeName") == "Sports":
            return attr.get("valueName")
    return None


def athlete_position(athlete: dict) -> str:
    for attr in athlete.get("attributes", []):
        if attr.get("typeName") == "Position":
            return attr.get("valueName", "")
    return ""


# Volleyball position groups. These are the same five codes the Kinexon practice-load
# pipeline uses, so a reader can join force plate results to practice load without a
# translation table in between.
VOLLEYBALL_POSITION_GROUPS = {
    "setter": "S",
    "outside hitter": "OH",
    "opposite hitter": "OPP",
    "opposite": "OPP",
    "middle blocker": "MB",
    "middle": "MB",
    "l/ds": "DSL",
    "libero": "DSL",
    "defensive specialist": "DSL",
    "ds": "DSL",
}


def volleyball_position_group(position: str) -> str:
    return VOLLEYBALL_POSITION_GROUPS.get((position or "").strip().lower(), "")

def reattribute_from_vald(
    db_path: str = "data/forceplate.db",
    sport: str | None = None,
    reset_sport: bool = False,
    client: "VALDClient | None" = None,
) -> dict:
    """Fill in athlete_name / sport / position on rows the football pull left blank.

    The football pipeline pulls every CMJ test on the tenant but only resolves names for
    football-rostered athletes, so roughly two thirds of `raw_tests` arrived with a
    blank `athlete_name` and no way to tell which sport it belonged to. The VALD roster
    knows, and this walks it.

    `reset_sport=True` clears the column first. Use it once, to undo any prior blanket
    assumption about what the unattributed rows were; afterwards anything still NULL is
    genuinely unresolvable (an athlete deleted from the tenant, most likely) rather than
    mislabelled.
    """
    client = client or VALDClient()
    conn = get_connection(db_path)
    init_schema(conn)

    if reset_sport:
        conn.execute("UPDATE raw_tests SET sport = NULL")
        conn.execute("UPDATE imtp_tests SET sport = NULL")

    athletes = client.get_athletes()
    if sport:
        athletes = [a for a in athletes if sports.athlete_sport(a) == sport]

    # One roster temp table joined once per target table. Looping the roster and
    # issuing an UPDATE per athlete would mean ~1,600 full scans of a 1.25M-row table.

#!/bin/bash
# One command for the VALD ForceDecks pull — the 10:10 + 16:40 launchd job and any manual run.
#   ./pull_vald.sh
# Runs run_pipeline.py (football CMJ + IMTP pull, then classify) into data/forceplate.db.
# VALD filters tests by modifiedFromUtc, so each run asks only for tests changed since
# 3 days before the last successful run (or 7 days before the newest stored test_date
# when there is no receipt). Upserts make re-fetching a window safe.
# Every run leaves logs/last_run.json; a failure appends one line to the alert log that
# the Claude Code SessionStart hook surfaces. Exit code = the last pipeline attempt's.
# After a successful pipeline run it writes Parquet snapshots of every table to Google
# Drive (export_snapshot.py) so the Windows laptop can read the data. An export failure
# alerts and is recorded in the receipt under snapshot_export, but never changes the exit code.
set -u

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PY="${VALD_PULL_PYTHON:-$HERE/.venv/bin/python}"
SNAPSHOT_DIR="${VALD_PULL_SNAPSHOT_DIR:-}"  # empty: $ATHLETE_SNAPSHOT_DIR, else Drive
DB="$HERE/data/forceplate.db"
RECEIPT="$HERE/logs/last_run.json"
ALERT_LOG="${VALD_PULL_ALERT_LOG:-$HOME/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log}"
ATTEMPTS=2
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

stamp() { date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z'; }

alert() {
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$ALERT_LOG")"
  printf '[%s] vald-pull: %s — see %s\n' "$(stamp)" "$1" "$RECEIPT" >> "$ALERT_LOG"
}

if ! cd "$HERE"; then
  alert "error exit=1 cannot cd to $HERE"
  exit 1
fi
mkdir -p "$HERE/logs"

started="$(stamp)"
echo "[$started] vald pull start"

from="$("$PY" -c '
import json, sys, duckdb
from datetime import date, timedelta
receipt, db = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
try:
    last = json.load(open(receipt)).get("last_success_date")
    if last:
        print((date.fromisoformat(last) - timedelta(days=3)).isoformat()); sys.exit()
except Exception:
    pass
c = duckdb.connect(db, read_only=True)
d = c.execute("select max(test_date) from raw_tests").fetchone()[0]
print((d - timedelta(days=7)).isoformat())
' "$RECEIPT" "$DB")"
if [ -z "$from" ]; then
  alert "error exit=1 could not work out the window start"
  exit 1
fi
echo "from $from"

rc=1
attempt=0
while [ "$attempt" -lt "$ATTEMPTS" ]; do
  attempt=$((attempt + 1))
  "$PY" run_pipeline.py --from-date "$from"
  rc=$?
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && break
  echo "attempt $attempt failed (exit=$rc)"
  [ "$attempt" -lt "$ATTEMPTS" ] && sleep 120
done

"$PY" -c '
import json, sys, duckdb
started, rc, attempts, frm, db, out = sys.argv[1:7]
prev = {}
try:
    prev = json.load(open(out))
except Exception:
    pass
raw = cls = None
try:
    c = duckdb.connect(db, read_only=True)
    raw = c.execute("select max(test_date) from raw_tests").fetchone()[0]
    cls = c.execute("select max(test_date) from classified_athletes").fetchone()[0]
except Exception:
    pass
ok = rc == "0"
json.dump({
    "started_at": started,
    "status": "ok" if ok else "error",
    "exit_code": int(rc),
    "attempts": int(attempts),
    "from_date": frm,
    "db_path": db,
    "db_newest_raw_test_date": raw.isoformat() if raw else None,
    "db_newest_classified_date": cls.isoformat() if cls else None,
    "last_success_date": started[:10] if ok else prev.get("last_success_date"),
}, open(out, "w"), indent=2)
' "$started" "$rc" "$attempt" "$from" "$DB" "$RECEIPT"

if [ "$rc" -ne 0 ]; then
  alert "error exit=$rc after $attempt attempt(s)"
fi

# Parquet snapshots for Windows (successful pulls only). Logged + alerted, never fatal.
if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  if [ -n "$SNAPSHOT_DIR" ]; then
    "$PY" "$HERE/export_snapshot.py" --db "$DB" --receipt "$RECEIPT" --dest "$SNAPSHOT_DIR"
  else
    "$PY" "$HERE/export_snapshot.py" --db "$DB" --receipt "$RECEIPT"
  fi
  xrc=$?
  echo "[$(stamp)] snapshot export exit=$xrc"
  if [ "$xrc" -ne 0 ]; then
    alert "snapshot-export exit=$xrc (pull succeeded; Windows snapshot not refreshed)"
  fi
fi
echo "[$(stamp)] vald pull end exit=$rc"
exit "$rc"

#   ./pull_vald.sh
# Runs run_pipeline.py (football CMJ + IMTP pull, then classify) into data/forceplate.db.
# VALD filters tests by modifiedFromUtc, so each run asks only for tests changed since
# 3 days before the last successful run (or 7 days before the newest stored test_date
# when there is no receipt). Upserts make re-fetching a window safe.
# Every run leaves logs/last_run.json; a failure appends one line to the alert log that
# the Claude Code SessionStart hook surfaces. Exit code = the last pipeline attempt's.
# After a successful pipeline run it writes Parquet snapshots of every table to Google
# Drive (export_snapshot.py) so the Windows laptop can read the data. An export failure
# alerts and is recorded in the receipt under snapshot_export, but never changes the exit code.
set -u

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PY="${VALD_PULL_PYTHON:-$HERE/.venv/bin/python}"
SNAPSHOT_DIR="${VALD_PULL_SNAPSHOT_DIR:-}"  # empty: $ATHLETE_SNAPSHOT_DIR, else Drive
DB="$HERE/data/forceplate.db"
RECEIPT="$HERE/logs/last_run.json"
ALERT_LOG="${VALD_PULL_ALERT_LOG:-$HOME/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log}"
ATTEMPTS=2
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

stamp() { date '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z'; }

alert() {
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$ALERT_LOG")"
  printf '[%s] vald-pull: %s — see %s\n' "$(stamp)" "$1" "$RECEIPT" >> "$ALERT_LOG"
}

if ! cd "$HERE"; then
  alert "error exit=1 cannot cd to $HERE"
  exit 1
fi
mkdir -p "$HERE/logs"

started="$(stamp)"
echo "[$started] vald pull start"

from="$("$PY" -c '
import json, sys, duckdb
from datetime import date, timedelta
receipt, db = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
try:
    last = json.load(open(receipt)).get("last_success_date")
    if last:
        print((date.fromisoformat(last) - timedelta(days=3)).isoformat()); sys.exit()
except Exception:
    pass
c = duckdb.connect(db, read_only=True)
d = c.execute("select max(test_date) from raw_tests").fetchone()[0]
print((d - timedelta(days=7)).isoformat())
' "$RECEIPT" "$DB")"

  alert "error exit=1 could not work out the window start"
  exit 1
fi
echo "from $from"

rc=1
attempt=0
while [ "$attempt" -lt "$ATTEMPTS" ]; do
  attempt=$((attempt + 1))
  "$PY" run_pipeline.py --from-date "$from"

raw = cls = None

if [ "$rc" -eq 0 ]; then
  if [ -n "$SNAPSHOT_DIR" ]; then
    "$PY" "$HERE/export_snapshot.py" --db "$DB" --receipt "$RECEIPT" --dest "$SNAPSHOT_DIR"
  else
    "$PY" "$HERE/export_snapshot.py" --db "$DB" --receipt "$RECEIPT"

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

This is a decision support system for analyzing Countermovement Jump (CMJ) force plate data collected via **VALD ForceDecks** for **Football** athletes. It classifies athletes, diagnoses movement deficits, and drives training prescriptions throughout the competitive season.

**Status:** Implemented. Full pipeline built across 15 tasks. 120 tests passing across 9 test files. V3 dashboard with 5-tab layout, SSC/plyo staging, phase composites, microcycle prescriptions, and physio flags.

## Commands

```bash
python -m pytest -v                           # run all tests
python -m pytest tests/test_engine.py -v      # run a single test file
python run_pipeline.py --dry-run              # verify API auth, no DB writes
python run_pipeline.py                        # pull + classify + store
python run_pipeline.py --report               # pull + classify + HTML dashboard
python run_pipeline.py --report-only          # HTML dashboard from existing DB
python run_pipeline.py --reset-baseline <ID>  # reset one athlete's baseline
python run_pipeline.py --diagnose             # show all athletes and inclusion/exclusion reason
python run_pipeline.py --diagnose "Name"      # search for a specific athlete by name

# Multi-sport central store
python run_pipeline.py --sport-cmj Volleyball # ingest one sport's CMJ, no classification
python run_pipeline.py --reattribute          # fill name/sport/position from VALD roster
python run_pipeline.py --reattribute Volleyball --reset-sport

# Rep-level football CMJ: every rep, metric, limb -> cmj_trials (+ metric_definitions labels)
python run_pipeline.py --cmj-trials --from-date 2025-10-20 --recorded-from 2025-10-20 --recorded-to 2026-10-20
```

`raw_tests` keeps one rep (the first trial the API lists) and bilateral values only. `cmj_trials`
keeps all of them, in the unit named on each row; join `metric_definitions` on `result_id`, not name.

## The database is a multi-sport central store

`raw_tests` holds CMJ data for **every sport on the Baylor VALD tenant**, not just
football, and always has — `run_cmj_raw_backfill` pulls every CMJ test on the tenant and
only ever resolved *names* for football-rostered athletes. That is why 65% of rows
arrived with a blank `athlete_name`. Of 1.25M rows only ~163k are football.

`sport` (added 2026-08) makes that explicit. Attribution comes from
`reattribute_from_vald()`, which walks the VALD roster and fills in name, sport,
position and position group. After the first full run:

| sport | rows | athletes |
|---|---:|---:|
| (unattributed — profile deleted from tenant) | 374,232 | 231 |
| Archive | 328,961 | 317 |
| Football | 162,600 | 107 |
| Acrobatics and Tumbling | 100,417 | 50 |
| Volleyball | 43,216 | 18 |
| …15 more sports | | |

**Never backfill `sport` to 'Football'.** It is the obvious shortcut and it is wrong —
it relabels every other sport. NULL means "not yet attributed", which is honest and
lets a query decide. Other systems (e.g. `Kinexon_Volleyball`) read this database
read-only rather than keeping their own copy.

### Sport boundaries in the classification engine

`raw_tests` is sport-agnostic. `classified_athletes` is **football only** by
construction: the 4-step engine scores athletes against NFL normative percentiles keyed
by football position, and no equivalent normative table exists for volleyball.
`--sport-cmj` therefore stops at raw metrics. Anything built on a non-football sport
must compare an athlete to her own history, which needs no external norm.

## Scheduled pull and Parquet snapshots (Mac owns forceplate.db)

`data/forceplate.db` is a **DuckDB** file despite the `.db` name. The Mac is its only writer: launchd
`com.keystone.valdpull` runs `pull_vald.sh` (10:10 + 16:40). After a successful pipeline run,
`pull_vald.sh` runs `export_snapshot.py` (logic in `src/snapshot.py`), which opens the DB read-only and
writes Parquet to Google Drive for Windows and other read-only consumers:

- **Where:** `$ATHLETE_SNAPSHOT_DIR/vald/`, else `00_Primary_Storage_Drive/athlete-snapshots/vald/`
  (Mac `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-eric.rash11@gmail.com/My Drive/...`, Windows `G:\My Drive\...`).
  One file per table: `raw_tests` (all sports, ~12 MB), `classified_athletes`, `imtp_tests`,
  `athlete_baselines`, plus `manifest.json` (per table: rows, bytes, written_at UTC, machine, newest
  `test_date` / `baseline_date`). No table is skipped (there are no log tables); transient `_`-prefixed
  work tables such as `_vald_roster` are.
- **Windows reads, never writes:**
  `duckdb.sql("select * from 'G:/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/athlete-snapshots/vald/raw_tests.parquet'")`.
- **Atomic:** written as `<table>.parquet.tmp`, then renamed.
- **Stale-writer guard:** a table whose snapshot already records more rows than this DB is refused
  (exit 3; the other tables are still written) unless `--force`. After `--reset-baseline` shrinks
  `athlete_baselines`, run `export_snapshot.py --force` by hand.
- **Failure:** exit 0 ok · 1 error · 2 no DB / Drive not mounted · 3 refused. Non-zero alerts
  (`snapshot-export exit=N`) and is recorded in `logs/last_run.json` under `snapshot_export`; the pull's
  exit code is unchanged. The export prints table names and counts only, never names.
- **By hand (Mac):** `.venv/bin/python export_snapshot.py --dry-run`, then without `--dry-run`.

## Project Structure

```
src/
  ingest/vald_client.py    # VALD ForceDecks API client (OAuth2 + REST)
  ingest/pipeline.py       # Data pull orchestration, football athlete filter
  classify/engine.py       # 4-step classification orchestrator
  classify/asymmetry.py    # Step 1: bilateral asymmetry screen
  classify/mrsi.py         # Step 2: mRSI tier classification
  classify/eccentric.py    # Step 3: eccentric profile confirmation
  classify/p1p2.py         # Step 4: concentric impulse quadrant
  report/html_dashboard.py # Jinja2 HTML report generator + SVG radar charts
  report/templates/dashboard.html.j2  # Dashboard Jinja2 template (Baylor branded)
  report/templates/dashboard.html.j2.bak  # Pre-redesign template backup
  db.py                    # DuckDB schema + queries
config/thresholds.yaml     # Position-specific normative percentiles
run_pipeline.py            # CLI entry point
```

## Domain Model: 4-Step Classification Pipeline

The core logic selects 42 metrics from 239 available in VALD ForceDecks:

**Step 1 — Asymmetry Screen** ([src/classify/asymmetry.py](src/classify/asymmetry.py))
Bilateral Asymmetry Braking Impulse: <10% pass, 10–15% caution, >15% flag (restrict + 48h clinical eval)

**Step 2 — mRSI Primary Classification** ([src/classify/mrsi.py](src/classify/mrsi.py))
mRSI vs position-specific P25/P75: ≥P75 → gold, ≥P25 → purple, <P25 → white

**Step 3 — Eccentric Profile Confirmation** ([src/classify/eccentric.py](src/classify/eccentric.py))
EPF/BM ≥2.5x AND peak_power_bm ≥P75 → gold_confirm; EPF/BM <2.0x → ecc_flag (downgrades gold→purple)

**Step 4 — P1/P2 Concentric Impulse Quadrant** ([src/classify/p1p2.py](src/classify/p1p2.py))
CI sorted into Q1–Q4 by position norms; P1/P2 sub-quadrant via 62%/38% proportional split of quartile midpoint

## Athlete Classification Tiers

| Tier | Threshold | Color |
|------|-----------|-------|
| Elite | ≥ P75 | GOLD |
| Average | P25–P75 | PURPLE |
| Developmental | < P25 | WHITE |

## Implementation Gotchas

- **HTML dashboard (V3)**: `--report` generates a single self-contained HTML file (`reports/YYYY-MM-DD_team_dashboard.html`) with 5 tabs: Overview (position-grouped roster), Profiles (radar + phase composite bars), Training Rx (MD-1–MD-4 microcycles + station groups), Plyo Stages (Wilmot continuum by SSC regime), Physio Flags (landing risk + localStorage notes). Baylor branding (#001a0d bg, #FECB00 accents). A persistent summary stats bar shows squad-wide tier/flag counts above all tabs. `team_name` is set to `"Baylor Football"` in `render_dashboard()`.
- **DuckDB SQL**: Use `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and `ON CONFLICT (pk) DO UPDATE SET excluded.*` — SQLite syntax (`INSERT OR IGNORE`, `INSERT OR REPLACE`) does not work
- **PyJWT 2.x**: `jwt.decode()` requires `algorithms=["RS256", "HS256"]` even when `verify_signature: False`
- **kaleido**: Pin `kaleido>=0.2,<1.0` — v1.x requires an external Chrome install; v0.x is self-contained
- **Readiness flags**: Consecutive logic (both tests must exceed threshold) is checked BEFORE single-test red (>10%) so the >15% consecutive-red path remains reachable
- **P1/P2 medians**: Derived dynamically from quartile CI boundaries (`ci_mid * 0.62` / `* 0.38`), not hardcoded global values
- **Eccentric metric split**: `Eccentric Peak Force / BM [N/kg]` is used for the 2.5x/2.0x EPF gates in Step 3; `Eccentric Peak Power / BM [W/kg]` is stored separately for display
- **Baseline management**: Dashboard trend compares current test vs average of first 4 tests in current season per athlete. Athletes with <4 tests show "Establishing baseline (N/4 tests)". Classification baselines (`athlete_baselines` table) set on first occurrence only; never auto-updated. Manual reset via CLI flags only.
- **Movement type units**: API returns Eccentric Duration in **seconds** (not ms) and Countermovement Depth as **negative cm**. `_movement_type()` uses `abs()` on depth and second-based thresholds (0.450s / 0.600s). Missing data shows "Unknown" instead of defaulting to "Balanced". Current thresholds produce a skewed distribution (~93% Balanced) — most fast athletes don't also go deep (>38cm), and most slow athletes still have moderate depth.
- **Template display conversions**: Eccentric Duration is stored in seconds but displayed as `× 1000` ms in the template. Countermovement Depth is stored as negative cm but displayed as `| abs |` positive cm. Bodyweight is stored in kg but displayed as `× 2.20462` lbs. These conversions happen in `dashboard.html.j2`, not in Python.
- **Movement strategy badges**: Color-coded by type in the template via `badge-move-{{ type | lower | replace(' ', '-') }}` classes — Balanced (green), Fast-Deep (cyan), Slow-Shallow (orange), Slow-Deep (purple), Unknown (gray).
- **Config path in classify modules**: Use `Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "config" / "thresholds.yaml"` — relative paths break when tests run from project root
- **Radar SVG layout**: 360×400 viewBox (width × height), radius 140. `_SVG_H = 400` gives room for both value labels and legend. Value labels use `_TWO_DECIMAL_KEYS` set for RSI-modified and FT:CT (2 decimal places); all others get 1 decimal place.
- **Position grouping**: `POSITION_ORDER` constant in `html_dashboard.py` controls roster group order. Filter JS hides empty position groups; sort operates within each `.card-grid`, not across groups.
- **Prescriptions schema (V3)**: `config/thresholds.yaml` prescriptions are now nested dicts keyed by `group → quadrant → {text, plyo_station, md4, md3, md2, md1}`. `p1p2.py` reads `prescriptions[group][quadrant]["text"]`. `html_dashboard.py` reads `md4`–`md1` and `plyo_station` from the same dict in `build_athlete_context()`. Old flat key format (`gold.low_p1: "..."`) is no longer valid.
- **SSC regime**: Computed in `html_dashboard.py::_ssc_regime()` from `Contraction Time` (seconds) using `ssc_thresholds` in `thresholds.yaml`. Fast SSC < 0.150s, Slow SSC > 0.250s, Mixed SSC in between. Falls back to "Unknown" when CT is missing.
- **Plyo staging**: `_plyo_stage(ssc, final_group, ci_quartile)` returns `(stage: int, locked: bool)`. Ceiling by SSC: Fast=5, Mixed=3, Slow=2. Stage bumped by CI quartile within ceiling. `locked=True` when stage ≥ 4 and SSC is not Fast.
- **Phase composites**: `_phase_composites()` returns 5 normalized delta dicts `{label, delta, positive}`. Delta = `(value - p50) / (p75 - p25)`, clamped to [-2, 2]. Landing composite is inverted (lower PLF/BM is better). Requires `ft_ct` and `plf_bm` thresholds in `thresholds.yaml` per position.
- **Physio flags**: `_physio_flags()` checks `plf_bm_flag`, `jh_rel_plf_flag`, and `asymmetry_braking.caution` per position. Returns list of `{label, value, threshold, exceeded}`. Physio notes saved to `localStorage` in browser, keyed by `physio_note_<athlete_id>`.
- **Encoding in thresholds.yaml**: All prescription text must use ASCII dashes (`-`), not en-dashes or em-dashes — non-ASCII dashes cause mojibake in browser rendering.
- **Stale deps**: `streamlit`, `plotly`, `xhtml2pdf` remain in `requirements.txt` but are unused after the move to pure Jinja2 HTML. Safe to remove.
- **Python 3.14**: Project runs on Python 3.14.0 — some packages may have compatibility warnings

## VALD API Gotchas

- **Team ID**: `4828f39e-7bb5-4178-8b25-1d9371fa9d09` (Baylor University) — use this exact UUID in `.env`, not the encoded `ZIEhQbmiBQkubFg==` string
- **Football filter**: Athletes have `attributes[typeName=="Sports"].valueName == "Football"` — 107 of 1,583 total athletes. Filter applied in `pipeline.py:is_football_athlete()`
- **Metric names**: No unit suffixes in API — `"RSI-modified"` not `"RSI-modified [m/s]"`, `"Eccentric Peak Force / BM"` not `"Eccentric Peak Force / BM [N/kg]"`, etc.
- **RSI-modified scale**: API returns value × 100 (e.g., 73.0 = 0.73 m/s). Apply `resultUnitScaleFactor = 0.01` from `/resultdefinitions`. Only factors < 1 are applied; time metrics (×1000 to ms) are left as-is since raw values are already in seconds. Duration metrics (Eccentric Duration, Concentric Duration, Contraction Time) are stored in **seconds** in `raw_tests`.
- **Asymmetry from bilateral trials**: Within a `limb="Both"` trial, each result has a `result.limb` field: `"Trial"` (combined), `"Left"`, `"Right"`, `"Asym"` (asymmetry %). Stored as `"Eccentric Braking Impulse Asymmetry"` key.
- **Result definitions endpoint**: `GET /resultdefinitions` → 512 metric definitions with `resultName`, `resultUnit`, `resultUnitScaleFactor`. Cached in `VALDClient.get_result_definitions()`.
- **Landing Stiffness**: API name is `"Landing Stiffness"` (confirmed via `/resultdefinitions`), `supportsAsymmetry: true`.
- **Per-test trials call**: One `GET /v2019q3/teams/{teamId}/tests/{testId}/trials` per test — 2,730 calls for 2026 season data takes ~8 minutes.

## Key Metrics (42 total)

**Tier 1 — Performance Outputs (3 metrics)**
- Jump Height, RSI-modified, Flight Time:Contraction Time

**Tier 2 — Braking Phase (5 metrics)**
- ECC Deceleration RFD (`EDRFD/BM` — most sensitive metric for deceleration injury risk)
- ECC Mean Braking Force, Eccentric Mean Force, Force at Zero Velocity, Force at Zero Velocity/BM

**Tier 2 — Propulsive Phase (10 metrics)**
- Concentric Impulse, Concentric Impulse @100ms, Con Impulse 100ms:Total
- Concentric RFD, Concentric RFD @100ms, P1/P2 Concentric Impulse, P2:P1 Ratio, Con Mean Force/BM

**Tier 2 — Landing Phase (6 metrics)**
- Peak Landing Force, Peak Landing Force/BM, JH-Relative Peak Landing Force
- Landing RFD, Landing RFD 50ms, Landing Stiffness

**Tier 3 — Movement Strategy (9 metrics)**
- Eccentric Duration, Concentric Duration, Countermovement Depth
- ECC:CON Duration Ratio, ECC:CON Mean Force Ratio, ECC:CON Peak Power Ratio
- Contraction Time, CMJ Stiffness, Lower-Limb Stiffness

**Metadata (1):** Body Mass

## Primary Decision Thresholds (NFL Normative Percentiles by Position)

All thresholds are in `config/thresholds.yaml` keyed by full position name. Each position gets its own P25/P50/P75 — not a pooled group average.

**P1/P2 Concentric Impulse Quartile boundaries (per position):**
- Q1: 0 → q1_max | Q2: q1_max → q2_max | Q3: q2_max → q3_max | Q4: q3_max → q3_max×1.15

## Stakeholder Hierarchy (Tactical Hierarchy of Injury Mitigation)

Controls ~90% of fatigue via training design (dose controllers):
1. **Technical Staff** (High control) — duration, pitch size, session intensity, match minutes
2. **Sports Scientist** (Medium control) — GPS/HR data interpretation, load monitoring
3. **S&C Coach** (Medium control) — tissue tolerance via eccentric loading, plyometrics
4. **Medical Staff** (Low control) — reactive; screening, inflammation management

## Football-Specific Normative Data (Fully Available)

The VALD 2024-25 NFL and NCAA Football Report provides P5/P25/P50/P75/P95 values for all CMJ metrics across 10 positions for both NFL and NCAA athletes:

**Positions covered:** Defensive Back, Defensive Line, Linebacker, Offensive Line, Quarterback, Running Back, Tight End, Wide Receiver, Special Teams, Kicker/Punter

**Position group mapping for classification:**
- `skill`: DB, LB, QB, RB, WR, TE, ST, K/P
- `big`: DL, OL

**Key NFL medians for reference (skill positions):**
| Metric | DB | WR | RB | LB |
|--------|----|----|----|----|
| Jump Height Imp-Mom (cm) | 47.9 | 48.0 | 45.5 | 43.7 |
| RSI-Modified (m/s) | 0.74 | 0.74 | 0.69 | 0.66 |
| FT:CT | 0.94 | 0.94 | 0.90 | 0.87 |
| Peak Power/BM (W/kg) | 67.4 | 67.5 | 64.5 | 61.3 |
| EDRFD/BM (N/s/kg) | 119 | 116 | 114 | 108 |
| Ecc Peak Power/BM (W/kg) | 24.1 | 23.6 | 22.4 | 23.8 |

**Key NFL medians for reference (big positions):**
| Metric | OL | DL |
|--------|----|----|
| Jump Height Imp-Mom (cm) | 33.1 | 37.7 |
| RSI-Modified (m/s) | 0.47 | 0.56 |
| Peak Power/BM (W/kg) | 49.7 | 55.1 |
| EDRFD/BM (N/s/kg) | 74 | 89 |

## Documentation

- [`docs/coaches_manual.md`](docs/coaches_manual.md) — V3 user manual: 5-tab dashboard navigation, classification interpretation, SSC/plyo staging guide, and role-specific best-use workflows
- [`docs/coaches_manual_v1.md`](docs/coaches_manual_v1.md) — Original (pre-V3) manual preserved for reference
- [`docs/session.md`](docs/session.md) — Session context log for development changes

## Reference Documents

All reference materials are in [`ContextBackgroundInfo/`](ContextBackgroundInfo/):

- [`CMJ Force Plate Thresholding-Pentheny.pdf`](ContextBackgroundInfo/CMJ%20Force%20Plate%20Thresholding-Pentheny.pdf) — Primary threshold framework, GOLD/PURPLE/WHITE classification system
- [`2026-03-20_CMJ_MetricSelectionRationale.pdf`](ContextBackgroundInfo/2026-03-20_CMJ_MetricSelectionRationale.pdf) — Rationale for 42-metric selection, 4-step hybrid model detail
- [`TacticalHierarchy.pdf`](ContextBackgroundInfo/TacticalHierarchy.pdf) — Organizational hierarchy for injury mitigation decisions
- [`valdperformance-com-Beyond the Numbers with Strength-IQ.pdf`](ContextBackgroundInfo/valdperformance-com-Beyond%20the%20Numbers%20with%20Strength-IQ.pdf) — Strength IQ reliability methodology
- [`VALD Normative Data Report – 2024-25 NFL and NCAA Football Report.pdf`](ContextBackgroundInfo/VALD%20Normative%20Data%20Report%20%E2%80%93%202024-25%20NFL%20and%20NCAA%20Football%20Report.pdf) — Full P5/P25/P50/P75/P95 normative tables for all CMJ metrics by position (NFL + NCAA)

- **Eccentric metric split**: `Eccentric Peak Force / BM [N/kg]` is used for the 2.5x/2.0x EPF gates in Step 3; `Eccentric Peak Power / BM [W/kg]` is stored separately for display
- **Baseline management**: Dashboard trend compares current test vs average of first 4 tests in current season per athlete. Athletes with <4 tests show "Establishing baseline (N/4 tests)". Classification baselines (`athlete_baselines` table) set on first occurrence only; never auto-updated. Manual reset via CLI flags only.
- **Movement type units**: API returns Eccentric Duration in **seconds** (not ms) and Countermovement Depth as **negative cm**. `_movement_type()` uses `abs()` on depth and second-based thresholds (0.450s / 0.600s). Missing data shows "Unknown" instead of defaulting to "Balanced". Current thresholds produce a skewed distribution (~93% Balanced) — most fast athletes don't also go deep (>38cm), and most slow athletes still have moderate depth.
- **Template display conversions**: Eccentric Duration is stored in seconds but displayed as `× 1000` ms in the template. Countermovement Depth is stored as negative cm but displayed as `| abs |` positive cm. Bodyweight is stored in kg but displayed as `× 2.20462` lbs. These conversions happen in `dashboard.html.j2`, not in Python.
- **Movement strategy badges**: Color-coded by type in the template via `badge-move-{{ type | lower | replace(' ', '-') }}` classes — Balanced (green), Fast-Deep (cyan), Slow-Shallow (orange), Slow-Deep (purple), Unknown (gray).
- **Config path in classify modules**: Use `Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "config" / "thresholds.yaml"` — relative paths break when tests run from project root
- **Radar SVG layout**: 360×400 viewBox (width × height), radius 140. `_SVG_H = 400` gives room for both value labels and legend. Value labels use `_TWO_DECIMAL_KEYS` set for RSI-modified and FT:CT (2 decimal places); all others get 1 decimal place.
- **Position grouping**: `POSITION_ORDER` constant in `html_dashboard.py` controls roster group order. Filter JS hides empty position groups; sort operates within each `.card-grid`, not across groups.
- **Prescriptions schema (V3)**: `config/thresholds.yaml` prescriptions are now nested dicts keyed by `group → quadrant → {text, plyo_station, md4, md3, md2, md1}`. `p1p2.py` reads `prescriptions[group][quadrant]["text"]`. `html_dashboard.py` reads `md4`–`md1` and `plyo_station` from the same dict in `build_athlete_context()`. Old flat key format (`gold.low_p1: "..."`) is no longer valid.
- **SSC regime**: Computed in `html_dashboard.py::_ssc_regime()` from `Contraction Time` (seconds) using `ssc_thresholds` in `thresholds.yaml`. Fast SSC < 0.150s, Slow SSC > 0.250s, Mixed SSC in between. Falls back to "Unknown" when CT is missing.
- **Plyo staging**: `_plyo_stage(ssc, final_group, ci_quartile)` returns `(stage: int, locked: bool)`. Ceiling by SSC: Fast=5, Mixed=3, Slow=2. Stage bumped by CI quartile within ceiling. `locked=True` when stage ≥ 4 and SSC is not Fast.
- **Phase composites**: `_phase_composites()` returns 5 normalized delta dicts `{label, delta, positive}`. Delta = `(value - p50) / (p75 - p25)`, clamped to [-2, 2]. Landing composite is inverted (lower PLF/BM is better). Requires `ft_ct` and `plf_bm` thresholds in `thresholds.yaml` per position.
- **Physio flags**: `_physio_flags()` checks `plf_bm_flag`, `jh_rel_plf_flag`, and `asymmetry_braking.caution` per position. Returns list of `{label, value, threshold, exceeded}`. Physio notes saved to `localStorage` in browser, keyed by `physio_note_<athlete_id>`.
- **Encoding in thresholds.yaml**: All prescription text must use ASCII dashes (`-`), not en-dashes or em-dashes — non-ASCII dashes cause mojibake in browser rendering.
- **Stale deps**: `streamlit`, `plotly`, `xhtml2pdf` remain in `requirements.txt` but are unused after the move to pure Jinja2 HTML. Safe to remove.
- **Python 3.14**: Project runs on Python 3.14.0 — some packages may have compatibility warnings

## VALD API Gotchas

- **Team ID**: `4828f39e-7bb5-4178-8b25-1d9371fa9d09` (Baylor University) — use this exact UUID in `.env`, not the encoded `ZIEhQbmiBQkubFg==` string
- **Football filter**: Athletes have `attributes[typeName=="Sports"].valueName == "Football"` — 107 of 1,583 total athletes. Filter applied in `pipeline.py:is_football_athlete()`
- **Metric names**: No unit suffixes in API — `"RSI-modified"` not `"RSI-modified [m/s]"`, `"Eccentric Peak Force / BM"` not `"Eccentric Peak Force / BM [N/kg]"`, etc.
- **RSI-modified scale**: API returns value × 100 (e.g., 73.0 = 0.73 m/s). Apply `resultUnitScaleFactor = 0.01` from `/resultdefinitions`. Only factors < 1 are applied; time metrics (×1000 to ms) are left as-is since raw values are already in seconds. Duration metrics (Eccentric Duration, Concentric Duration, Contraction Time) are stored in **seconds** in `raw_tests`.
- **Asymmetry from bilateral trials**: Within a `limb="Both"` trial, each result has a `result.limb` field: `"Trial"` (combined), `"Left"`, `"Right"`, `"Asym"` (asymmetry %). Stored as `"Eccentric Braking Impulse Asymmetry"` key.
- **Result definitions endpoint**: `GET /resultdefinitions` → 512 metric definitions with `resultName`, `resultUnit`, `resultUnitScaleFactor`. Cached in `VALDClient.get_result_definitions()`.
- **Landing Stiffness**: API name is `"Landing Stiffness"` (confirmed via `/resultdefinitions`), `supportsAsymmetry: true`.
- **Per-test trials call**: One `GET /v2019q3/teams/{teamId}/tests/{testId}/trials` per test — 2,730 calls for 2026 season data takes ~8 minutes.

## Key Metrics (42 total)

**Tier 1 — Performance Outputs (3 metrics)**
- Jump Height, RSI-modified, Flight Time:Contraction Time

**Tier 2 — Braking Phase (5 metrics)**
- ECC Deceleration RFD (`EDRFD/BM` — most sensitive metric for deceleration injury risk)
- ECC Mean Braking Force, Eccentric Mean Force, Force at Zero Velocity, Force at Zero Velocity/BM

**Tier 2 — Propulsive Phase (10 metrics)**
- Concentric Impulse, Concentric Impulse @100ms, Con Impulse 100ms:Total
- Concentric RFD, Concentric RFD @100ms, P1/P2 Concentric Impulse, P2:P1 Ratio, Con Mean Force/BM

**Tier 2 — Landing Phase (6 metrics)**
- Peak Landing Force, Peak Landing Force/BM, JH-Relative Peak Landing Force
- Landing RFD, Landing RFD 50ms, Landing Stiffness

**Tier 3 — Movement Strategy (9 metrics)**
- Eccentric Duration, Concentric Duration, Countermovement Depth
- ECC:CON Duration Ratio, ECC:CON Mean Force Ratio, ECC:CON Peak Power Ratio
- Contraction Time, CMJ Stiffness, Lower-Limb Stiffness

**Metadata (1):** Body Mass

## Primary Decision Thresholds (NFL Normative Percentiles by Position)

All thresholds are in `config/thresholds.yaml` keyed by full position name. Each position gets its own P25/P50/P75 — not a pooled group average.

**P1/P2 Concentric Impulse Quartile boundaries (per position):**
- Q1: 0 → q1_max | Q2: q1_max → q2_max | Q3: q2_max → q3_max | Q4: q3_max → q3_max×1.15

## Stakeholder Hierarchy (Tactical Hierarchy of Injury Mitigation)

Controls ~90% of fatigue via training design (dose controllers):
1. **Technical Staff** (High control) — duration, pitch size, session intensity, match minutes
2. **Sports Scientist** (Medium control) — GPS/HR data interpretation, load monitoring
3. **S&C Coach** (Medium control) — tissue tolerance via eccentric loading, plyometrics
4. **Medical Staff** (Low control) — reactive; screening, inflammation management

## Football-Specific Normative Data (Fully Available)

The VALD 2024-25 NFL and NCAA Football Report provides P5/P25/P50/P75/P95 values for all CMJ metrics across 10 positions for both NFL and NCAA athletes:

**Positions covered:** Defensive Back, Defensive Line, Linebacker, Offensive Line, Quarterback, Running Back, Tight End, Wide Receiver, Special Teams, Kicker/Punter

**Position group mapping for classification:**
- `skill`: DB, LB, QB, RB, WR, TE, ST, K/P
- `big`: DL, OL

|--------|----|----|

def get_tests(self, from_date: str, test_type: str = "CMJ") -> list[dict]:
        """GET /tests — paginated by modifiedFromUtc. Repeats until 204 No Content.

        Returns only tests of the given testType. Each test contains testId, profileId,
        recordedDateUtc, weight, and empty extendedParameters (metrics are on trials).
        """
        all_tests = []
        modified_from = f"{from_date}T00:00:00.000Z" if "T" not in from_date else from_date

        while True:
            resp = self._get(
                f"{self._region_url}/tests",
                headers=self._headers(),
                params={
                    "tenantId": self._team_id,
                    "modifiedFromUtc": modified_from,
                },
            )
            if resp.status_code == 204:
                break
            resp.raise_for_status()
            data = resp.json()
            tests = data.get("tests", [])
            if not tests:
                break

            # Filter to requested test type
            typed = [t for t in tests if t.get("testType") == test_type]
            all_tests.extend(typed)

            # Paginate: advance to last modifiedDateUtc in this batch
            modified_from = tests[-1]["modifiedDateUtc"]

        return all_tests

from common import *
import yaml
df = sessions("2025-08-01")
cfg = yaml.safe_load(open("/Users/kristinarash/DEV/Football/PerformanceSnapshot/snapshot.yaml"))
c2g = {c: g for g, cs in cfg["positions"].items() for c in cs}
df = df[(df.ptype=="practice") & (df.session_date.astype(str).str[5:7] >= "08") & (df.total_duration_s >= 40*60)].copy()
df["grp"] = df.position.map(c2g)
df = df[df.grp.notna()]
df["impacts_high_pm"] = df.impacts_high / (df.total_duration_s/60)
df["contacts_pm"] = df.total_contacts / (df.total_duration_s/60)
df["window"] = df.session_date.astype(str).str[:4]
M = ["total_player_load","total_distance_m","total_accel_load","explosive_efforts","total_contacts","impacts_high","pl_veryhigh",
     "player_load_per_minute","meterage_per_minute","accel_density","explosive_ratio_avg","ima_per_minute","impacts_high_pm","contacts_pm","pl_veryhigh_per_min","max_velocity_ms" if False else "high_speed_distance_m"]
def icc1(d, k):
    g = d.groupby("name")[k]; n = g.count(); n = n[n>=5]
    d = d[d.name.isin(n.index)]; g = d.groupby("name")[k]
    grand = d[k].mean(); k0 = n.mean()
    msb = (g.count()*(g.mean()-grand)**2).sum()/(len(n)-1)
    msw = ((d[k]-d.groupby("name")[k].transform("mean"))**2).sum()/(len(d)-len(n))
    return (msb-msw)/(msb+(k0-1)*msw)
out=[]
nsess = df.groupby(["name","window"]).size().median()
for k in M:
    d = df[["name","grp","window",k,"total_duration_s"]].dropna()
    r = icc1(d, k)
    win_rel = nsess*r/(1+(nsess-1)*r)
    am = d.groupby(["name","grp","window"])[k].mean().reset_index()
    eta = am.groupby("grp")[k].apply(lambda s: len(s)*(s.mean()-am[k].mean())**2).sum()/((am[k]-am[k].mean())**2).sum()
    d["dc"] = d.total_duration_s - d.groupby("name").total_duration_s.transform("mean")
    d["kc"] = d[k] - d.groupby("name")[k].transform("mean")
    dur = d[["dc","kc"]].corr().iloc[0,1]
    cv = (d.groupby("name")[k].std()/d.groupby("name")[k].mean()).median()
    out.append((k, round(r,2), round(win_rel,2), round(eta,2), round(dur,2), f"{cv:.0%}"))
print(f"in-season practices >=40 min, 2025+2026: {len(df)} athlete-sessions, median {nsess:.0f} sessions per athlete-season")
print(pd.DataFrame(out, columns=["metric","ICC session","reliab. of season mean","position eta2","r with duration (within athlete)","within-athlete CV"]).to_string(index=False))
am = df.groupby(["name","window"])[M].mean()
cm = am.corr(method="spearman").round(2)
print("\nSpearman between athlete-season means (selected):")
sel = ["total_player_load","total_distance_m","explosive_efforts","total_contacts","player_load_per_minute","meterage_per_minute","ima_per_minute","impacts_high_pm","explosive_ratio_avg","accel_density"]
print(cm.loc[sel, sel].to_string())
print("\nduplicates check (session-level r):", round(df[["explosive_efforts"]].join(sessions("2025-08-01")[["total_high_ima"]]).corr().iloc[0,1],3) if False else "")

    print(f"  {a} == {b}: {(d0[a]==d0[b]).mean():.1%} rows identical")

- **Activities filter:** `start_time` / `end_time` are **Unix timestamps** (not ISO 8601)
- **Stats endpoint:** `POST /stats` with `filters: [{name: "activity_id", comparison: "=", values: [uuid]}]`
- **Stats source:** `cached_stats`, `group_by: ["athlete"]`
- **`POST /stats` works** and returns 200 — `bake_status=unprocessed` does NOT block it
- **Do NOT use:** `maximum_velocity`, `high_speed_running_distance`, `athlete_max_velocity`, `percentage_max_velocity`, `deceleration_density` — return 0 or wrong slugs for this account
- **`max_vel`** = session max velocity in **mph** — multiply × 0.44704 to store as m/s
- **`velocity_band3_total_distance`** = HSD (75–90% of max vel), in meters
- **`velocity_band4–8_total_distance`** = sprint bands; bands 5–8 always return 0 for Baylor
- **Full parameter list** available at `GET /parameters` — 1,829 slugs. Saved to `logs/all_parameters.json`.

### Metric field mapping (API → DB)
| API field | DB column | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `average_player_load` | `total_player_load` | session average per athlete, not cumulative |
| `total_distance` | `total_distance_m` | stored in meters; displayed in yards |
| `max_vel` | `max_velocity_ms` | API value is mph; stored m/s (`× 0.44704`); displayed mph |
| `velocity_band3_total_distance` | `vb3_distance_m` + `high_speed_distance_m` | raw band stored; derived metric computed from config |
| `velocity_band4–8_total_distance` | `vb4–vb8_distance_m` + `sprint_distance_m` | raw bands stored; derived metric summed from config |
| `velocity_band3/4_total_effort_count` | `vb3_effort_count`, `vb4_effort_count` | # entries into HSD/sprint zones |
| `acceleration_density` | `accel_density` | |
| `explosive_efforts` | `explosive_efforts` | = `total_high_ima` (same values) |
| `total_duration` | `total_duration_s` | session duration in seconds |
| `total_acceleration_load` | `total_accel_load` | |
| `average_velocity` | `average_velocity_ms` | stored m/s |
| `meterage_per_minute` | `meterage_per_minute` | |
| `player_load_per_minute` | `player_load_per_minute` | |
| `explosive_ratio_(avg)` | `explosive_ratio_avg` | |
| `ima_band3_accel/decel/right/left_count` | `ima_high_accel/decel/right/left` | high-intensity IMA counts |
| `high_ima_accel/decel` | `ima_high_accel_decel` | combined high IMA accel+decel |
| `total_high/medium/low_ima(_movements)` | `total_high/medium/low_ima` | IMA movement tier totals |
| `ima/min`, `total_high_ima/min`, `total_high_ima_(avg)` | `ima_per_minute`, `total_high_ima_per_min`, `total_high_ima_avg` | IMA rate/avg metrics |
| `impacts_low/med/high` | `impacts_low/med/high` | collision/contact event counts |
| `impact_low_(avg)`, `impacts_med_(avg)`, `impacts_high_(avg)` | `impacts_low/med/high_avg` | impact averages |
| `pl_low/med/high/veryhigh` | `pl_low/med/high/veryhigh` | player load band totals |
| `pl_med_(avg)` | `pl_high_avg` | ⚠️ Catapult name/slug mismatch — slug says "med" but value is PL_High (Avg) |
| `pl_veryhigh_(avg)`, `pl_veryhigh/min` | `pl_veryhigh_avg`, `pl_veryhigh_per_min` | |
| `total_lineman_contact_count` | `total_contacts` | all players (not just linemen despite name) |
| `total_qb_throw_count` | `total_throws` | QB-specific; zero for all non-QB athletes |

### Velocity band storage architecture
Raw band columns (`vb3_distance_m`–`vb8_distance_m`) are stored as DB ground truth. Derived metrics (`high_speed_distance_m`, `sprint_distance_m`) are computed at ingest from `config.yaml` `metrics.derived` band assignments — same principle as m→yds/m/s→mph unit conversions. To redefine HSD or Sprint zones: edit `config.yaml` → run `python backfill_velocity.py`. No code changes needed.

### Athlete roster API fields (`GET /athletes`)
- **Name:** `first_name` + `last_name` (separate fields — no `full_name`, `name`, or `displayName`)
- **Jersey:** `jersey` field (string, may be non-numeric e.g. `"DBB"`) — parse to `int`, store `NULL` if non-numeric
- **Position:** `position_name` (e.g. `"DL"`) preferred over `position` (single-letter code e.g. `"D"`)

import os, sys, requests, statistics as st
from dotenv import load_dotenv
load_dotenv(sys.argv[1])
T = os.environ["CATAPULT_TOKEN"].strip()
H = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {T}", "Content-Type": "application/json", "Accept": "application/json"}
for act in sys.argv[2:]:
    body = {"filters": [{"name": "activity_id", "comparison": "=", "values": [act]}],
            "parameters": ["total_player_load","average_player_load","player_load_per_minute","total_duration","field_time"],
            "group_by": ["athlete"], "source": "cached_stats"}
    r = requests.post("https://connect-us.catapultsports.com/api/v6/stats", headers=H, json=body, timeout=60)
    j = r.json(); rows = j if isinstance(j, list) else j.get("data", [])
    f = lambda x, k: (float(x[k]) if x.get(k) not in (None, "") else None)
    ok = [x for x in rows if f(x,"total_player_load") and f(x,"player_load_per_minute") and f(x,"total_duration")]
    rat = [f(x,"player_load_per_minute")*f(x,"total_duration")/60/f(x,"total_player_load") for x in ok]
    ratft = [f(x,"player_load_per_minute")*f(x,"field_time")/60/f(x,"total_player_load") for x in ok if f(x,"field_time")]
    print(f"{act[:8]} status {r.status_code} athletes {len(rows)} | true total median {st.median(f(x,'total_player_load') for x in ok):.0f}"
          f" | derived/true (total_duration) median {st.median(rat):.3f} range {min(rat):.3f}-{max(rat):.3f}"
          + (f" | (field_time) {st.median(ratft):.3f}" if ratft else "")
          + f" | true/average {st.median(f(x,'total_player_load')/f(x,'average_player_load') for x in ok if f(x,'average_player_load')):.1f}")

from common import *
import yaml
cfg = yaml.safe_load(open("/Users/kristinarash/DEV/Football/PerformanceSnapshot/snapshot.yaml"))
c2g = {c: g for g, cs in cfg["positions"].items() for c in cs}
df = sessions("2025-08-01")
df = df[(df.ptype=="practice") & (df.session_date.astype(str).str[5:7] >= "08") & (df.total_duration_s >= 40*60)].copy()
df["grp"] = df.position.map(c2g); df = df[df.grp.notna()]
mins = df.total_duration_s/60
df["player_load_TOTAL"] = df.player_load_per_minute * mins
df["contacts_pm"] = df.total_contacts / mins
df["impacts_high_pm"] = df.impacts_high / mins
df["window"] = df.session_date.astype(str).str[:4]
VOL = ["player_load_TOTAL","total_distance_m","explosive_efforts","total_contacts","impacts_high"]
INT = ["player_load_per_minute","meterage_per_minute","ima_per_minute","explosive_ratio_avg","contacts_pm","impacts_high_pm"]
def icc1(d, k):
    n = d.groupby("name")[k].count(); n = n[n>=5]; d = d[d.name.isin(n.index)]
    g = d.groupby("name")[k]; grand = d[k].mean(); k0 = n.mean()
    msb = (g.count()*(g.mean()-grand)**2).sum()/(len(n)-1)
    msw = ((d[k]-g.transform("mean"))**2).sum()/(len(d)-len(n))
    return (msb-msw)/(msb+(k0-1)*msw)
nsess = df.groupby(["name","window"]).size().median()
out=[]
for k in VOL+INT:
    d = df[["name","grp","window",k,"total_duration_s"]].dropna()
    r = icc1(d, k); rel = nsess*r/(1+(nsess-1)*r)
    am = d.groupby(["name","grp","window"])[k].mean().reset_index()
    eta = am.groupby("grp")[k].apply(lambda s: len(s)*(s.mean()-am[k].mean())**2).sum()/((am[k]-am[k].mean())**2).sum()
    dc = d.total_duration_s - d.groupby("name").total_duration_s.transform("mean"); kc = d[k]-d.groupby("name")[k].transform("mean")
    out.append(("volume" if k in VOL else "intensity", k, round(r,2), round(rel,2), round(eta,2), round(np.corrcoef(dc,kc)[0,1],2)))
print(pd.DataFrame(out, columns=["role","metric","ICC session","reliab season mean","position eta2","r duration"]).to_string(index=False))
am = df.groupby(["name","window"])[VOL+INT].mean().corr(method="spearman").round(2)
print(am.to_string())
gm = df.groupby("grp")[["player_load_TOTAL","player_load_per_minute","ima_per_minute","contacts_pm","explosive_efforts","total_contacts"]].median().round(2)
print(gm.to_string())

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
